extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: MATHVISTA is a benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks. It consists of 6,141 examples, derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu (UCLA; Microsoft Research, Redmond); Hritik Bansal (UCLA); Tony Xia (UCLA); Jiacheng Liu (University of Washington); Chunyuan Li (Microsoft Research, Redmond); Hannaneh Hajishirzi (University of Washington); Hao Cheng (Microsoft Research, Redmond); Kai-Wei Chang (UCLA); Michel Galley (Microsoft Research, Redmond); Jianfeng Gao (Microsoft Research, Redmond)
extraction.citeAs: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao. MATHVISTA: EVALUATING MATHEMATICAL REASONING OF FOUNDATION MODELS IN VISUAL CONTEXTS. ICLR 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was assembled by collecting examples from 28 existing multimodal datasets using heuristic rules and manual filtering, and by creating three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) sourced from online learning platforms, online education resources, and academic papers on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 28 existing multimodal datasets (including 9 MathQA and 19 VQA datasets), puzzle test figures from online learning platforms, and academic papers released on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: All questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and further refined through a rigorous review process. Initially, each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers. Then, these discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team, ensuring a consensus was reached on each example.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: majority voting; discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team, ensuring a consensus was reached
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: There may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals; Annotations lack a unified format and structure due to the heterogeneity of sources.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: AI agents with strong mathematical reasoning capabilities in visual contexts have a wide range of realworld applications, such as solving complex problems in educational disciplines, helping analysts with logical queries about statistical data, and assisting in theorem proving and scientific discovery in advanced research fields.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Facilitate the development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios; Evaluate the research progress of LLMs and LMMs, especially their capabilities in solving rigorous reasoning tasks.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors will maintain an online evaluation platform, maintain the datasets by refining potential data noise in response to community feedback, and evolve the leaderboard in response to new models.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure a balanced representation of each source. Additionally, split-level resampling was used for the testmini set by randomly sampling questions with a threshold number of 4 for each source dataset, then randomly sampling the remaining questions based on their proportion in the entire set.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Heuristic rules were designed to automatically filter and select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates, specifically selecting examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words in the questions.
